launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.summary: Discovery Park is Seattle's 560-acre natural park of meadow, forest, bluff, tidal beaches, active dunes, wildlife habitat, cultural history, and West Point Lighthouse.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.hours: Discovery Park follows posted Seattle park hours. The Visitor Center is closed until summer 2027; parking, beach access, cultural facilities, restrooms, and shuttle use separate conditions.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.cost: General park, trails, beaches, viewpoints, play area, and seasonal shuttle are free. Programs, events, and nearby services may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.parking: Use the North, East, or South general-use lots. The beach lot by West Point Lighthouse is ADA-placard only; there is no general parking past the East Lot.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.arrival: Choose the East Lot for the closed Visitor Center area and meadow, North Lot for Daybreak Star, or South Lot for Loop Trail and beach hiking. General drivers cannot park at the lighthouse.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available at selected developed areas, but the closed Visitor Center reduces indoor services. Plan around parking areas and cultural-facility hours.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.accessibility: The beach parking lot is restricted to ADA placards. Trails range from developed routes to steep bluff and beach paths; the seasonal shuttle accepts service animals and strollers.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.dogs: Follow posted leash and beach rules. Pets are not allowed on the seasonal shuttle, and wildlife, cultural grounds, narrow trails, and tidal areas require control.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.family: Meadows, play area, Loop Trail sections, lighthouse views, and the seasonal shuttle work for families, but long distances and steep beach approaches require planning.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.transit: Metro routes 24 and 33 reach park edges; route 33 serves the North Lot. The free summer shuttle runs Thursday through Sunday through September 5, 2026.
launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.need: The Visitor Center is closed until summer 2027. The summer shuttle runs 11 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with the last beach departure at 5:15; check tides, rain, wind, trail work, and return time.

launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.address: 7201 East Green Lake Drive N, Seattle, WA 98115
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.summary: Green Lake Park surrounds a busy urban lake with a 2.8-mile paved loop, two swimming beaches, wading pool, playground, sports, fishing, boating, and community facilities.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.hours: The park is open daily 4 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. Beaches, wading pool, Evans Pool, community center, boat programs, restrooms, and fields use separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.cost: Park, loop, playground, beaches, wading pool when open, and general recreation are free. Pool, programs, rentals, reservations, and parking may cost.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.parking: Small lots and curb parking are distributed around the lake and fill quickly. Choose East Beach, West Beach, fields, or Small Craft Center before navigating.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.arrival: East Green Lake is closest to the community center, Evans Pool, wading pool, play area, and East Beach. West Green Lake serves the theater side and longer-season beach.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.restrooms: Restrooms are concentrated near the community center, beaches, play area, and active facilities and may not keep full park hours.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.accessibility: The paved 2.8-mile loop is broadly usable, with high congestion. Pedestrians use the inner lane; wheels use the outer one-way lane with a 10 mph limit.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed on a maximum five-foot leash and controlled on the busy loop. Dogs are excluded from play areas, designated swimming beaches, and wading pool.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.family: The play area, seasonal wading pool, beaches, fields, and flat loop offer variety, but beach lifeguards and water play are seasonal and weather dependent.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.transit: Frequent buses serve Green Lake neighborhoods. Pick a stop near the intended side because walking the full loop adds 2.8 miles.
launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.need: In 2026 East Beach closes after August 23 while West Beach remains lifeguarded through September 7. Check algae, bacteria, lifeguards, wading-pool weather, and crowd conditions.

launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.summary: Gas Works Park combines preserved industrial structures, Kite Hill, a sundial, Play Barn, picnic lawns, skyline views, and Burke-Gilman Trail access on Lake Union.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.hours: Gas Works Park is open daily 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Major events can restrict lots, lawns, paths, and picnic areas.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.cost: Park, viewpoints, play area, lawns, and trail connections are free. Reservations, permits, events, food, and transportation may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.parking: The park lot is limited and fills quickly on sunny days and events. Cycling via the Burke-Gilman Trail, transit, walking, or rideshare are often easier.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.arrival: Use the Northlake Way lot for the Play Barn and central paths. Continue toward Kite Hill and the lake viewpoint on foot; event closures can alter circulation.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.restrooms: Public restrooms and drinking fountains are listed park amenities near developed central areas; verify event access before relying on them.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.accessibility: Developed routes connect parking, lawns, viewpoints, and play areas, while Kite Hill grades, crowds, wet grass, and event fencing vary.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and out of play areas and restricted shoreline. Pick up waste and control pets around crowded lawns and bicycle traffic.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.family: The Play Barn, Kite Hill, sundial, lawns, and skyline views are family-friendly, but preserved machinery is not general climbing equipment and the lake is off limits.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.transit: The Burke-Gilman Trail runs past the parking lot, and buses serve Wallingford and Fremont approaches.
launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.need: No swimming, fishing, wading, boat launching, or water entry is allowed because lake sediment contains hazardous substances. Check the 2026 large-event calendar before visiting.

launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.address: 5900 Lake Washington Boulevard S, Seattle, WA 98118
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.summary: Seward Park is a 300-acre Lake Washington peninsula with old-growth forest, a 2.4-mile shore loop, beach, playground, amphitheater, art studio, trails, and Mount Rainier views.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.hours: Park grounds follow posted Seattle park hours. Swimming beach, restrooms, art studio, permits, and events use separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.cost: Park, shore loop, forest trails, playground, beach access, and general recreation are free. Programs, rentals, permits, and events may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.parking: Lots are distributed near the beach, amphitheater, and park entrance and fill on warm weekends. Route to the exact activity area.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.arrival: Use the main Lake Washington Boulevard entrance for beach, playground, and Shore Loop Road. Forest trails climb into the interior from the loop.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.restrooms: Restrooms are concentrated near the beach and developed recreation areas; interior forest trails do not provide dependable facilities.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.accessibility: The paved shore loop and developed beach area are the most usable routes. Interior trails include roots, grades, mud, and narrower natural surfaces.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.dogs: Dogs must follow leash rules and are not allowed on designated swimming beaches or children's play areas.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.family: The playground, paved lake loop, seasonal swimming beach, picnic areas, and short forest walks support a full family outing.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.transit: Buses serve nearby Rainier Valley and Lake Washington Boulevard approaches, though the peninsula still requires walking.
launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.need: The lifeguarded beach runs June 27 through September 7 in 2026, generally noon to 7 weekdays and 11 a.m. to 7 weekends. Check water quality, wildfire smoke, storms, and beach status.

launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.summary: Washington Park Arboretum is a free 230-acre living collection with Azalea Way, Pacific Connections, woodland paths, waterfront trails, seasonal color, and the ticketed Seattle Japanese Garden.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.hours: Arboretum grounds are open daily from dawn to 8 p.m. Graham Visitors Center is generally Wednesday through Sunday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; exterior restrooms are open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.cost: Arboretum grounds and trails are free. Seattle Japanese Garden admission, programs, tours, events, and purchases may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.parking: Free lots and curb areas are distributed near Graham Visitors Center, Pacific Connections, playfield, and Japanese Garden and can fill during peak bloom.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.arrival: Start at Graham Visitors Center for maps and Azalea Way, use the south end for Japanese Garden, or route to Pacific Connections for southern collections.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.restrooms: Exterior restrooms at Graham Visitors Center are open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Additional facilities are at Pacific Connections, Washington Park Playfield, and Japanese Garden.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.accessibility: Developed routes serve the Visitor Center and major gardens, while woodland and waterfront paths vary in grade, roots, mud, and seasonal flooding.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.dogs: Leashed dogs may use general arboretum paths where posted but are restricted from the Seattle Japanese Garden and sensitive collection areas.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.family: Wide paths, seasonal plants, waterfront exploration, open lawns, and short loops work well; water edges and garden rules require supervision.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.transit: Buses serve Madison Street and nearby neighborhoods. The Arboretum is long north-to-south, so choose the stop closest to the desired collection.
launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.need: Grounds stay open later than staffed facilities. Check Visitor Center staffing, restroom hours, Japanese Garden admission, rain, mud, high wind, and seasonal bloom crowds.

launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.summary: Volunteer Park is a historic Olmsted landscape with Conservatory, Seattle Asian Art Museum, water tower, reservoir, playground, seasonal wading pool, gardens, tennis, and amphitheater.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.hours: Park grounds follow posted Seattle park hours. Conservatory, museum, water tower, wading pool, restrooms, and events use separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.cost: General park, playground, gardens, water tower grounds, and wading pool when operating are free. Conservatory, museum, programs, and events may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.parking: Curb parking surrounds the park and fills during museum, conservatory, bloom, and event periods. Transit and walking are often easier.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.arrival: Use 15th Avenue E for the Conservatory and central park. The museum, playground, wading pool, water tower, and amphitheater occupy different sides.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.restrooms: Restrooms are near the playground and wading pool area and inside separately operated attractions during their hours.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.accessibility: Developed paths serve major attractions, but historic grades, steps, wet surfaces, and water tower access vary.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed and kept out of playground, wading pool, museum, conservatory, and planted display areas.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.family: The playground, weather-dependent wading pool, gardens, water tower, and conservatory make a varied family visit with separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.transit: Buses serve Capitol Hill and nearby 15th Avenue. Link light rail requires an uphill neighborhood walk or transfer.
launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.need: The 2026 wading pool operates daily noon to 7 through September 7 only on suitable warm-weather days. Check the morning hotline, attraction hours, and event occupation.

launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.summary: Kerry Park is Queen Anne's compact skyline overlook, known for Space Needle, Elliott Bay, downtown, ferry, and occasional Mount Rainier views, with a nearby lower play area.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.hours: Kerry Park is open daily 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. The overlook has no staffed visitor facility.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.cost: Overlook, sculpture, and general park access are free. Tours, parking, and nearby food cost separately.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.parking: There is no destination lot. Residential curb parking is scarce; avoid blocking driveways and use transit, walking, rideshare, or a legal space farther away.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.arrival: The classic overlook wall is on W Highland Drive. Bayview-Kinnear play area is downhill and separate from the main viewpoint.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.restrooms: Do not rely on a public restroom at this compact overlook. Use a confirmed-open facility before arriving, especially with children.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.accessibility: The main W Highland Drive overlook is compact and paved, but Queen Anne approaches are steep and the lower play area uses sloped neighborhood routes.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.dogs: Leash dogs and keep them controlled around the crowded overlook wall, sculpture, children, and residential edges.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.family: The view is a short stop rather than a full playground visit. Pair it with the lower Bayview-Kinnear play area if grades and time work.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.transit: Queen Anne buses stop within walking distance, but expect hills. Rideshare drop-off must respect the narrow residential street.
launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.need: Mount Rainier visibility is weather dependent. Sunset brings dense tripod and tour crowds; protect valuables, stay off private property, and do not expect food or restrooms.

launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.summary: Olympic Sculpture Park is a free nine-acre Seattle Art Museum waterfront landscape with monumental art, zigzag paths, lawns, beach habitat, Pavilion, and links to Myrtle Edwards Park.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.hours: May through September hours are 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.; October through April hours are 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Pavilion and programs use separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.cost: Outdoor park and sculpture access are free. Parking, food, tours, programs, and museum visits may cost.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.parking: There is no free park lot. Use transit, walking, cycling, rideshare, paid street parking, or nearby garages.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.arrival: Enter near Western Avenue and Broad Street for the PACCAR Pavilion and upper path, or approach from Myrtle Edwards Park along the waterfront trail.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.restrooms: Restroom availability is tied primarily to the PACCAR Pavilion and nearby facilities rather than every outdoor level; check Pavilion hours.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.accessibility: The main Z-shaped path provides a gradual developed route across grade changes, while beach and shoreline surfaces vary.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may pass through outdoor routes where posted; keep pets away from artworks, beach habitat, lawns during programs, and indoor Pavilion spaces.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.family: Large sculptures, lawns, trains, shoreline views, and the continuous path interest families, but artworks are not climbing equipment and the water edge requires supervision.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.transit: Buses, light rail connections, cycling, and walking from Seattle Center or downtown avoid limited parking.
launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.need: Respect art barriers, rail crossings, and shoreline habitat. Check seasonal hours, Pavilion access, event closures, rain, wind, smoke, and slippery surfaces.

launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.summary: Seattle's rebuilt Waterfront Park links a broad promenade, Overlook Walk, Pier 58 play, Pier 62 events and dock, Habitat Beach, public art, aquarium, Pike Place, ferries, and transit.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.hours: Waterfront Park is open daily 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Aquarium, vendors, ferries, elevators, restrooms, play areas, and events use separate schedules.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.cost: Promenade, Overlook Walk, public play spaces, piers, art, and many programs are free. Aquarium, food, parking, ferries, and attractions charge.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.parking: Paid street spaces and garages line downtown and Alaskan Way, but construction, cruise traffic, games, and events create delays. Transit and walking are usually easier.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.arrival: Use Overlook Walk from Pike Place for the elevated connection, Pier 58 for the jellyfish play structure, or Pier 62 for flexible events and floating dock.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.restrooms: The rebuilt park includes a public restroom, with additional facilities at Pier 62 and partner attractions during their hours. Identify the nearest open one along the long waterfront.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.accessibility: Wide promenades, elevators, Overlook Walk, and developed pier surfaces support accessible circulation, though outages and event layouts can alter routes.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed under posted rules; keep them controlled around play spaces, food, crowds, habitat, docks, and water edges.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.family: Pier 58's large play structure, Overlook Walk, Habitat Beach, aquarium surroundings, free games, and ferry views create a strong downtown family destination.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.transit: Light rail, buses, ferries, water taxi, seasonal Waterfront Shuttle, and walking from Pike Place all serve different sections.
launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.need: The waterfront is long and busy. Choose a meeting point, watch children near piers and traffic crossings, and check elevator, event, ferry, weather, and cruise conditions.

launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.summary: Golden Gardens Park is a Ballard shoreline destination with sandy beach, Olympic views, seasonal fire pits, bathhouse, playground, fishing pier, boat launch, wetlands, forest trails, and upper dog area.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.hours: May through September park hours are 4 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.; October through April hours are 4 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. Parking gates open at 7 a.m.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.cost: Beach, playground, trails, dog area, pier, and general access are free. Reservations, boat launch, parking where posted, food, and events may charge.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.parking: Large beach lots fill rapidly on warm weekends. Gates open at 7 a.m.; before then, legal public parking is available along Seaview Avenue NW.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.arrival: Use the lower beach lots for bathhouse, play area, fire pits, volleyball, pier, and launch. The off-leash dog area is in the upper northern park.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.restrooms: Restrooms are near the bathhouse and upper dog area, with operating hours that may differ from park grounds.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.accessibility: Developed beach and bathhouse areas include paved access, while sand, forest trails, rail crossings, and upper-lower grades vary.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.dogs: Dogs are not allowed on the beach or children's play area. Use the one-acre upper off-leash area; leash dogs elsewhere.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.family: Beach, play area, picnic space, trains, boats, and sunsets make a memorable outing, but cold water, rail crossings, fire pits, and crowds require supervision.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.transit: Buses reach Ballard approaches, with walking or cycling connections toward the park. The beach is downhill from many neighborhood stops.
launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.need: In 2026 fire pits operate May 22 through September 7 unless a burn ban applies. Use only installed pits, clean firewood, no alcohol, and extinguish with water by 9:30 p.m.
